errata.notes:
This errata is just for consistency

All others figures are not using open and end brackets, for example figure 24, 40, etc...

Technically if bracket are used, that could means we are in a closed struct, so in a card and the card is not valid as the RFC spec

By just remove first and last bracket, the figure is cleaner

This errata is for consistency

In section 2.2.1.1 The Name object is defined.
In figure 16,17,18,19 we give example of Name object
But the figure 18 is only the subpart of the Name object

With this update, all figures will be described the Name object consistently

errata.orig:
A CryptoKey object has all properties of the Resource (Section 1.4.4)
data type, with the following additional definition:

The @type property value MUST be "CryptoKey", if set.
errata.correct:
A CryptoKey object has all properties of the Resource (Section 1.4.4)
data type, with the following additional definition:

- The @type property value MUST be "CryptoKey", if set.

- The kind property is optional. Its enumerated (Section 1.7.5) values
   are:

  - link
  - embed
errata.notes:
I've noticed that CryptoKey is defined as a Resource but the CryptoKey "kind" is never defined.

The Resource specify that for kind: "The allowed values are defined in the property definition that makes use of the Resource type. Some property definitions may change this property from being optional to mandatory."


The proposed values in the corrected text are only suggestion from the example of the RFC

As values of "kind" type are registered with IANA we can see that the CryptoKey kind is not present at
https://www.iana.org/assignments/jscontact/jscontact.xhtml#jscontact-enum-values


If the CryptoKey kind is missing, I guess iana should also update the enum (email from the RFC: iana@iana.org)

errata.orig:
....
   organizationId        String                  Title   (Section 2.2.5)
   ....
   preferredLanguages    String[LanguagePref]    Card  (Section 2.3.4)
errata.correct:
....
   organizationId        Id                         Title   (Section 2.2.5)
   ....
   preferredLanguages    Id[LanguagePref]           Card  (Section 2.3.4)
errata.notes: Two properties listed in the "JSContact Properties Registry" entries (Table 2 of Section 3.5.2) differ from their corresponding definitions.
The language tag for Japanese is ja. jp is the country code of Japan.

The localization identified as Ukrainian contains Russian name forms.
Furthermore, the example should be considered a fragment of a JSContact card, as it lacks the mandatory properties required for a complete "Card" object.
The payload is not an OpenPGP public key, as indicated by "application/pgp-keys" media type, whose registration references RFC 3156.

errata.orig:
The registry entries sort numerically in ascending order by the
   "Major Version" column, and entries with equal "Major Version" sort
   numerically in ascending order by the "Minor Version" column.
errata.correct:
The registry entries sort numerically in ascending order by the
   "Major Version" column, and entries with equal "Major Version" sort
   numerically in ascending order by the "Highest Minor Version" column.
errata.notes: The sorting instructions refer to a nonexistent "Minor Version" column.

errata.orig:
The property value indicates that the middle name followed by both
      surnames should be used when sorting the name by surname.  The
      absence of "middle" indicates that the middle name on its own
      should be disregarded during sort.
errata.correct:
The property value indicates that the middle name followed by the
      surname should be used when sorting the name by surname. The
      absence of "given2" indicates that the middle name on its own
      should be disregarded during sort.
errata.notes:
The explanation of Figure 19 discusses the absence of "middle" from sortAs. The component kind defined by the RFC and used in the example is "given2".
The preceding sentence also refers to “both surnames”, although the example contains a single surname component with the value "Shou Chang". The explanation should refer to the middle name followed by the surname, without implying that the example contains two distinct surname components
